title: Private Access session status codes: where they appear, the component prefixes and the three classes

prose.text: {{where-shown}} The code names, their classes, descriptions and resolutions are the status codes of [[zpa/user-activity-log]], not restated here.

prose.label: In Diagnostics.
prose.text: {{internal-code-scope}} The page's own ICMP example shows an Info code as a status {{divergence:internal-code-scope-vs-icmp}}. Whether the LSS InternalReason field carries these Internal Reason codes is open {{gap:internal-reason-identity}}.

prose.label: Disagreements in the sources.
prose.text: Two entries of the LSS API example look shifted by one name {{divergence:hash-tbl-name-shift}}, and one row of the article repeats another row's description {{divergence:closed-from-client-copy}}. The thresholds that the rate-limit codes refer to are not stated {{gap:rate-limit-thresholds}}.

where-shown.statement: Private Access session status codes appear on the User Activity Diagnostics page; each table has its own search field and can be sorted by column.

quotes: Private Access (ZPA) session status codes appear on the User Activity Diagnostics page. Each table has its own search field and can be sorted by column.

prefixes.statement: Status codes are prefixed by the related Private Access component: AC (the App Connector), CA (the Central Authority), CLT (the Zscaler Client Connector), SE (the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge for Private Access) and ZPA BA (the Browser Access service).

quotes: Status codes are prefixed by the related Private Access component:
AC: The App Connector component.
CA: The Central Authority component.
CLT: The Zscaler Client Connector component.
SE: The Public Service Edge for Private Access or Private Service Edge for Private Access component.
ZPA BA: The Browser Access service.

internal-code-scope.statement: In User Activity diagnostics the Status Code is the status of the application request, and for errors and policy blocks the connection status name links to more about it. The Internal Status Code is the internal status reason, applies only to errors and policy blocks, and points to the session status codes article for the complete list of internal reasons per connection status.

quotes: Status Code: The status of the application request. For errors and policy blocks, you can click the connection status name to learn more about it.
Internal Status Code: The internal status reason.
This field only applies to errors and policy blocks. To see a complete list of internal reasons per connection status, see Understanding Private Access Session Status Codes.

internal-reason-identity.title: Whether the LSS InternalReason field holds the Internal Reason codes of the session status codes article
internal-reason-identity.detail: The article's column is named Internal Reason and the Diagnostics Internal Status Code links to it, which strengthens the reading, but no captured page says the LSS InternalReason field carries the same value. See also [[zpa.troubleshooting.log-fields:internal-reason-values]].

rate-limit-thresholds.title: The thresholds behind the rate-limit and workload-group codes
rate-limit-thresholds.detail: The article's rate-limit codes and the workload-group code refer to Ranges & Limitations without giving values. The ranges and limitations capture lists a per-second Microtunnel request limit and workload group limits, but nothing there says these are the thresholds the codes enforce. The preset waiting period of the too-many-failed-attempts code is undefined and its Resolution cell is empty.

internal-code-scope-vs-icmp.summary: The Internal Status Code applies only to errors and policy blocks, yet the Diagnostics page gives an Info code as an ICMP status example

positions.says: The Diagnostics page says the Internal Status Code applies only to errors and policy blocks.

quotes: This field only applies to errors and policy blocks.

positions.says: The same page gives BRK_MT_TERMINATED as the status an ICMP application might show as successful.

quotes: the status might show as successful (e.g., BRK_MT_TERMINATED)

positions.says: The session status codes article lists BRK_MT_TERMINATED in its Info table.

evidence.after: The following is a list of Info status codes:
quotes: | SE: Connection closed by Service Edge | BRK_MT_TERMINATED |

internal-code-scope-vs-icmp.impact: The page gives an Info code as the status of an ICMP application although it limits the Internal Status Code to errors and policy blocks; which of the two statements applies to an Info entry is not stated.

hash-tbl-name-shift.summary: The LSS API example names AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BRK_HASH_TBL_FULL 'Failed to process SAML response'; the article names that code differently

positions.says: In the LSS API example, the entry AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BRK_HASH_TBL_FULL is named 'SE: Failed to process SAML response'.

quotes: "name": "SE: Failed to process SAML response",

positions.says: The session status codes article names AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BRK_HASH_TBL_FULL 'AC: Service Edge database is full' and BRK_MT_AUTH_SAML_DECODE_FAIL 'SE: Failed to process SAML response'.

quotes: | AC: Service Edge database is full | AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BRK_HASH_TBL_FULL |
| SE: Failed to process SAML response | BRK_MT_AUTH_SAML_DECODE_FAIL |

hash-tbl-name-shift.impact: The example appears to have shifted one name onto the next entry: its AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_BRK_HASH_TBL_FULL carries the SAML name, and its BRK_MT_AUTH_SAML_DECODE_FAIL entry has no name. The two sources disagree and neither says which is wrong; check both before relying on either name for these two codes, including in the log type generated from the API example.

closed-from-client-copy.summary: BRK_MT_CLOSED_FROM_CLIENT and MT_CLOSED_TLS_CONN_GONE_AST_CLOSED have the same description

positions.says: The row named 'SE: Connection closed by Client Connector' (BRK_MT_CLOSED_FROM_CLIENT) describes a connection from the App Connector to the Service Edge being terminated, ending all application sessions for that App Connector.

quotes: | SE: Connection closed by Client Connector | BRK_MT_CLOSED_FROM_CLIENT | The connection from the App Connector to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge was terminated, resulting in the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge terminating all application sessions for that App Connector.

positions.says: The MT_CLOSED_TLS_CONN_GONE_AST_CLOSED row uses the same words for the App Connector's connection.

quotes: The connection from the App Connector to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge was terminated

closed-from-client-copy.impact: The name says the Client Connector closed the connection while the description speaks of the App Connector, so the description of BRK_MT_CLOSED_FROM_CLIENT cannot be relied on; the article does not say which is right.
